\section{Numbered galley}
An invented opening paragraph, set long enough that it wraps across
several lines of the narrow synthetic page it stands on, so the margin
count has body lines to attach to.
\begin{equation*}
e = m c^2
\end{equation*}
A second paragraph carries a mark.\footnote{The note is an insertion
and carries no number.}
\begin{figure}
A synthetic float body line.
\caption{A floated caption carries no number.}
\end{figure}
A third paragraph continues the invented prose so that the galley runs
past the first page boundary and the count is seen to continue rather
than restart.

A closing paragraph on the far side of the break, still counted in the
same running sequence from one.
